newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: OLYMPICS-END OF DREAM FOR SIX GAMES HOPEFULS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-END OF DREAM FOR SIX GAMES HOPEFULS.

text.p: The axe fell on the Olympic aspirations of six candidate cities for the 2004 Summer Games on Friday, leaving them with bruised egos, broken dreams and bitter frustration.

It also provoked some cries of foul, notably from Istanbul, who along with Lille, Rio de Janeiro, St Petersburg, San Juan and Seville failed to win a place among the five shortlisted candidates who will contest September's final selection for the venue of the Games.
Istanbul, already railing against the system of choosing Olympic venues before Friday's pre-selection procedure, hit out at what they suggested might be an anti-Moslem bias within the IOC.
"Never ever in the history of the Olympics has a Moslem country got to stage the Games," said Erman Tuncer of the Istanbul delegation.
"Are we seeing here the emergence of a Christian crusaders mentality? The two-billion-strong Moslem community of the world is being excluded from the Olympics."
The Russian city of St Petersburg pronounced itself nonplussed too by its exclusion from the shortlist on which Athens, Buenos Aires, Cape Town, Rome and Stockholm won places.
"Unfortunately the members probably have a very wrong picture of what is going on in Russia," said IOC Russian member Vitaly Smirnov.

"Our country is in a transitional period. If the criteria is stability then only a few countries could be chosen. We would not have had the Olympics in Korea in 1988 and to my mind it was one of the best."
Lille in northern France also felt a little aggrieved. "We thought we were strongly in contention with Stockholm for the fifth place," said Thierry Mabille of the French delegation.
"We have popular support in Lille and northern France for our bid but Stockholm has a lot of opposition. I do not think you can stage the Olympics where the people do not want it."

Rio de Janeiro brought out its sporting superstar Pele but still failed to score. "We have finished the first part of this game," he said. "Now we have to fight again with new vigour and win. We will be stronger next time."

Seville's delegation leader Enrique Moreno de la Cova said he felt his city's bid had been hampered by the fact that the Summer Games was staged in Spain as recently as 1992 when Barcelona were hosts.
"But we'll try harder next time," he added.
Fighting again was the only hope left for the disappointed six with all of them suggesting they may well come back and go through the process once more.
